To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incorporation of chitosan, choline chloride, and a triclosan-based derivative into a pigment printing formulation followed by printing on cotton/polyester blend (50/50 or 35/65), microwave curing (386 W for 3 min), and washing (20 cycles) resulted in the development of a novel pigment print with improved antibacterial activity.

the combined antimicrobial finishing and dyeing of cotton/polyesters can be achieved by incorporating the chitosan, triclosan and choline chloride with HBPAA/Ag-ZnO-NP hybrid into a pigment print paste and printing on cotton/polyester blend followed by microwave curing at 380 W for 5 mins.
the combined antimicrobial finishing and pigmented printing of the cotton/polyester fabric can be achieved using microwave irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of functionalized pigment print finishes for cotton/polyester blend fabrics.
the development of a novel approach for enhancing the antibacterial activity of the functionalized pigment prints and their application on cotton/polyester blended fabric.
the possibility of combining antimicrobial and coloration finishing in a one-step process, which can be used to produce functionalized pigment prints with improved antibacterial activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates the possibility to enhance the antimicrobial functionality and pigment printability of the cotton/polyester blend in a single step.

the combined antimicrobial finishing and dyeing of cotton/polyesters can be achieved by the inclusion of chitosan, choline chloride, triclosan derivatives, and HBPAA/Ag/ZnO-NPs hybrid into the pigment print formulations.

the combined antimicrobial finishing and pigmented printing of cotton/pet fabric is a viable and promising approach to produce multifunctional fabrics with excellent antibacterial properties and print quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by combining the antimicrobial functionality with the pigment printing, the functionalized prints can be used in a variety of applications such as in the medical field, in the textile industry, and in the home textile market, where antibacterial properties and color are both important.
the functionalized pigment prints could be an alternative to the conventional pigment printing and antibacterial finishing of cotton/poly polyester blends.

the incorporation of the antibacterial agents into the pigment printing formulation results in a significant enhancement of the antibacterial functionality, pigment printability, and durability of the pigment prints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the functionalized pigment prints have the ability to inhibit the growth of both G+ve and G-ve bacteria, which is an essential requirement for the production of functional textiles for healthcare purposes.
the functionalized pigment print can be used for the production of antimicrobial textile products.
the antimicrobial finishing and dyeing can be achieved by using one step process.
